scope: Documented corrections and retained variants; not certification of every Typikon chapter or every day

decisions.before: Fish on every ordinary Tuesday and Thursday of the Apostles fast and the initial Nativity-fast phase
decisions.after: Oil without fish on ordinary Tuesdays and Thursdays; feast allowances are evaluated separately

decisions.before: Doxology rank 5 ignored; vigil rank 3 treated as polyeleos on Wednesday/Friday; weekday feast fish allowances missing
decisions.after: Ranks 4/5 permit oil on Monday/Wednesday/Friday and fish on Tuesday/Thursday; ranks 1/2/3 permit fish before the Nativity forefeast. Ordinary ranks 6/7 confer no feast allowance
decisions.limits: Not applied to Great Lent, Dormition or the Nativity forefeast. Temple patronal feasts cannot be inferred from a general event title. Choice of actually celebrated service remains significant.

decisions.before: Both profiles permitted fish on every Wednesday/Friday after Bright Week and before Pentecost
decisions.after: Strict profile: oil on ordinary Wednesdays/Fridays, fish on Mid-Pentecost (Pascha +24) and Pascha leave-taking (+38). Explicit fixed fish feasts still take precedence. Parish profile retains the wider fish variant acknowledged in chapter 33

decisions.before: Ordinary Monday: boiled food without oil; doxology/polyeleos Monday: oil
decisions.after: Unchanged. Chapter 33 states dry eating on ordinary Mondays and fish for doxology Mondays; chapter 48 (November 14) excludes oil on ordinary Mondays and permits oil, not fish, for doxology/polyeleos Mondays. The existing combined profile is not being silently redefined as a literal implementation of chapter 33 alone
decisions.limits: The application is still a named composite table, not a complete service-dependent Typikon engine. Selecting one monastic practice for all ambiguous cases needs an explicit editorial rule.
